A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe the same work, Severing Spurious Correlations with Data Pruning. Their text, figures, table, mathematical expressions and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching Figure 2 across its relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original spurious-feature and pruning experiments on CIFAR-10S, CelebA, Hard ImageNet, Waterbirds and MultiNLI, including additional controlled experiments in Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and reports revised CelebA accuracies and an additional early-training observation in Figure 1.

M1.justification: Sections 5–6 retain the same prediction-error-based sample ranking and class-wise or group-wise pruning of difficult samples. No architecture, objective or algorithmic step changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same datasets, classification tasks and spurious-feature scenarios, including the appendix experiments. Figure 1b's additional training checkpoint does not introduce a different population, task or input environment.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains ERM, CnC, JTT, gDRO, DFRTr and PDE with identical dataset-specific participation. Figure 1b retains its existing identifiable-setting comparison with Liu et al. (2021); no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Figure 1b extends the regularization diagnostic with an unidentifiable-setting evaluation at epoch 2, alongside the retained observation now labeled epoch 1. This permits comparison with the identifiable setting at epoch 2. The main benchmark protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The added epoch-2 panel in Figure 1b checks whether samples with and without spurious features remain difficult to distinguish after further early training under weight decay 0.1. Other difficulty, pruning-sensitivity and appendix analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions already report graphical error bars and parenthetical uncertainty values in Table 1. Updated error-bar magnitudes and the additional panel do not change reporting practices; no new run counts, seeds or statistical procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Figure 1a revises several accuracies: female-with-eyeglasses accuracy changes from approximately 69% to 52% in the 10% panel and 31% to 20% in the 50% panel. Figure 1b adds epoch-2 results of approximately 79% and 74% for samples with and without spurious features. The qualitative conclusions, Table 1 and remaining results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The feature definitions, empirical-risk-minimization setup and sample-difficulty formula are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about unidentifiable spurious information, the influence of a few difficult samples and the effectiveness of data pruning. Figure 1 supplies revised support without changing those claims.

C2.justification: Section 3 qualifies regularization-based group separation as occurring 'early during training,' rather than simply 'during training.' This is a limited temporal refinement; the interpretations of weak-signal identification failure and the pruning mechanism remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 1b newly specifies the epochs of retained observations and explicitly gives weight decay 0.1 for the identifiable comparison. Section 3 identifies that comparison as Liu et al.'s CelebA setting. Appendix implementation details and the code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and related-work discussion are unchanged. Explicitly identifying the already cited Liu et al. (2021) comparison as CelebA clarifies its provenance without changing research positioning or novelty claims.

P1.justification: Section 3 receives localized wording additions about early training, the identifiable CelebA setting and the expanded figure reference. The section order and the remaining narrative, including the appendices, are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reformatted to accommodate three panels in part b instead of two, with explicit epoch and weight-decay labels. Figure 2 moves from page 4 to page 5, causing local text reflow. Other figures and the table retain their presentation.

improvement.justification: Figure 1b now provides an explicit epoch-2 comparison between identifiable and unidentifiable settings, improving transparency and modestly strengthening Section 3's motivating evidence. The benefit is limited: Figure 1a's numerical revisions are unexplained, while the method, main benchmark comparisons and appendices remain unchanged.
